# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.

"description": "Module format v1: a module's declaration is a mise config file, and the contract checker reads it (plan step 1, settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers" and "mise conf.d").

Layout (documentation convention, not checked: the checker only receives files): a module in source is a directory <name>/ holding <name>.toml (a mise config file, installed later as a conf.d drop-in, so its file name is the module name), README.md (what the module is, every key it sets, what it owns), optionally SKOGAI.md (agent-facing) and tests/.

Module name: the single key under `_.skogai`. It is the <name> used for the data record, the env prefix, task names and every cross-file rule. The file stem (file name without `.toml`) is compared with it only for name-mismatch. Files are recognised as modules by a case-sensitive `.toml` suffix with a non-empty stem; anything else is parsed as Markdown, as today.

Allowed top-level keys of a module toml: `_`, `env`, `tasks`. Any other top-level key (`tools`, `settings`, `vars`, `hooks`, `min_version`, ...) gives reason `unknown-section` (collected). Under `_`, only `skogai` is allowed; another key under `_` is also `unknown-section`.

Stopping parse stage (exactly one reason, nothing else is checked for that file, and the file takes no part in cross-file rules, as F001's parse reasons):
1. invalid-toml: `yq -p toml -o json` exits non-zero.
2. no-declaration: the parsed document is null (empty file) or not a table, or `_` is missing or not a table, or `_.skogai` is missing, not a table, or an empty table.
3. multiple-declarations: `_.skogai` has more than one key (even if one equals the stem).
4. not-a-mapping: the value of the single `_.skogai.<name>` key is not a table. An empty table is valid (every field is optional).

Collected reasons (any number, together with the existing field reasons, then the existing cross-file reasons):
- invalid-name: <name> does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (existing rule). An invalid name still takes part in duplicate-name, missing-dependency and ownership-conflict, as in F001.
- name-mismatch: <name> differs from the file stem. `hello.toml` with key `Hello` gets both invalid-name and name-mismatch.
- unknown-key: a key in the `_.skogai.<name>` table other than description, depends_on, reads, writes, owns, watches. `name` and `defaults` are unknown here (the name is the table key; defaults are `[env]`). Existing type and path rules apply to the allowed keys exactly as for Markdown.
- env-outside-prefix: `[env]` is optional. If present it must be a table (else wrong-type). Every key except mise's directive key `_` must start with the prefix `SKOGAI_<N>_`, where <N> is <name> uppercased with `-` removed (also computed for an invalid name), and be longer than the prefix (the bare prefix alone is outside). Values are not checked (types deferred).
- missing-task: `tasks` missing or not a table, or no `tasks.<name>`, or it is not a table, or it lacks a string `usage`, or it lacks `run` (a string or an array of strings). The usage string itself is not linted.
- task-outside-prefix: a key of `tasks` other than <name> that does not match `<name>:<sub>` with <sub> matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (one colon).
- unknown-section: see above.

"description": "Module format v1: a module's declaration is a mise config file, and the contract checker reads it (plan step 1, settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers" and "mise conf.d").

Layout (documentation convention, not checked: the checker only receives files): a module in source is a directory <name>/ holding <name>.toml (a mise config file, installed later as a conf.d drop-in, so its file name is the module name), README.md (what the module is, every key it sets, what it owns), optionally SKOGAI.md (agent-facing) and tests/.

Module name: the single key under `_.skogai`. It is the <name> used for the data record, the env prefix, task names and every cross-file rule. The file stem (file name without `.toml`) is compared with it only for name-mismatch. Files are recognised as modules by a case-sensitive `.toml` suffix with a non-empty stem; anything else is parsed as Markdown, as today.

Allowed top-level keys of a module toml: `_`, `env`, `tasks`. Any other top-level key (`tools`, `settings`, `vars`, `hooks`, `min_version`, ...) gives reason `unknown-section` (collected). Under `_`, only `skogai` is allowed; another key under `_` is also `unknown-section`.

Stopping parse stage (exactly one reason, nothing else is checked for that file, and the file takes no part in cross-file rules, as F001's parse reasons):
1. invalid-toml: `yq -p toml -o json` exits non-zero.
2. no-declaration: the parsed document is null (empty file) or not a table, or `_` is missing or not a table, or `_.skogai` is missing, not a table, or an empty table.
3. multiple-declarations: `_.skogai` has more than one key (even if one equals the stem).
4. not-a-mapping: the value of the single `_.skogai.<name>` key is not a table. An empty table is valid (every field is optional).

Collected reasons (any number, together with the existing field reasons, then the existing cross-file reasons):
- invalid-name: <name> does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (existing rule). An invalid name still takes part in duplicate-name, missing-dependency and ownership-conflict, as in F001.
- name-mismatch: <name> differs from the file stem. `hello.toml` with key `Hello` gets both invalid-name and name-mismatch.
- unknown-key: a key in the `_.skogai.<name>` table other than description, depends_on, reads, writes, owns, watches. `name` and `defaults` are unknown here (the name is the table key; defaults are `[env]`). Existing type and path rules apply to the allowed keys exactly as for Markdown.
- env-outside-prefix: `[env]` is optional. If present it must be a table (else wrong-type). Every key except mise's directive key `_` must start with the prefix `SKOGAI_<N>_`, where <N> is <name> uppercased with `-` removed (also computed for an invalid name), and be longer than the prefix (the bare prefix alone is outside). Values are not checked (types deferred).
- missing-task: `tasks` missing or not a table, or no `tasks.<name>`, or it is not a table, or it lacks a string `usage`, or it lacks `run` (a string or an array of strings). The usage string itself is not linted.
- task-outside-prefix: a key of `tasks` other than <name> that does not match `<name>:<sub>` with <sub> matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (one colon).
- unknown-section: see above.
Two modules whose prefixes collide (e.g. `a-b` and `ab`) are not detected in v1; docs/module.md lists it as open.

Implementation constraint: src/core/contract/usage.sh only (contract/argc.sh is frozen; no sed/awk). The record grows to {file, kind: "md"|"toml", parse, data, module} where `module` (toml only) carries what the module rules need (stem, top-level keys, env, tasks). VERDICTS may change: the field rules and cross-file rules are shared by both kinds; the allowed-key list for the relationship table differs by kind; the module-only rules apply when kind is toml. For Markdown input the output must stay byte-identical: `mise run test` and `mise run test:argc` stay green with no change to tests/contract.bats or tests/fixtures/contract/. Output shape ({file, verdict, reasons}, reasons sorted unique) and exit codes are unchanged. A TOML construct that mise accepts but yq rejects or decodes differently is judged by what yq yields; docs/module.md says so.

Example: examples/modules/hello/hello.toml and README.md:
  [env] SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = "{{ get_env(name='SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING', default='hi') }}"
  [_.skogai.hello] description, owns = ["greeting.txt"], writes = ["greeting.txt"]
  [tasks.hello] usage = 'arg "<who>"', run = 'echo "$SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING $usage_who" | tee greeting.txt'
It is valid. Live test (skipped only when `mise` is not on PATH): copy hello.toml into $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/p/.mise/conf.d/, then in that dir run mise under `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=<tmp> MISE_CONFIG_DIR MISE_SYSTEM_DIR MISE_DATA_DIR MISE_STATE_DIR MISE_CACHE_DIR` (all under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR) and `MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS=<that dir>`: `mise run -q hello world` exits 0, prints `hi world`, and leaves greeting.txt containing `hi world`; with `SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING=yo` added to that env it prints `yo world` (the caller's env beats the default).

Docs: docs/module.md describes the layout, the declaration, the naming rules and every reason, marked implemented/verified. It records these mise 2026.10.17 facts as verified by hand on 2026-11-07 (not by a test): conf.d is loaded at system (/etc/mise/conf.d), global (~/.config/mise/conf.d, follows MISE_CONFIG_DIR) and project (.mise/conf.d, .config/mise/conf.d) level; [env] merges key by key across layers, a later layer winning; a later layer's [tasks.x] replaces the whole task (so only the module's own file defines its tasks and relationships, and override files set [env] only); `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file, no merge; a plain [env] value beats the caller's env, a get_env default does not.

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type corpus + unit + integration. tests/module.bats with fixtures under tests/fixtures/module/{valid,invalid/<reason>}/, kept apart from tests/fixtures/contract/ because `mise run test:argc` runs contract.bats against the frozen argc checker. Every invalid/<reason>/ file produces exactly that one reason; every valid file is valid (at least: minimal empty table, full declaration, env with `_` directive key, extra `hello:sub` task). Multi-file case directories under valid/ and invalid/ follow F001's convention (one call per directory, compared byte for byte with expected.jsonl where present); one of them mixes a .md workorder and a .toml module that own the same path and expects ownership-conflict on both. Explicit cases for the overlaps: `Hello` key in hello.toml (invalid-name + name-mismatch), `_.skogai = "x"` (no-declaration), `_ = "x"` (no-declaration), zero-byte file (no-declaration), two keys one matching the stem (multiple-declarations only), `_.skogai.hello.name` (unknown-key). Tests isolate HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME as the suite does. `mise run test`, `mise run test:argc` and `.harness/init.sh smoke_test` pass.

Out of scope: install/uninstall (C), config get/set (B), run executing the mise task (D), depends_on at run time (E), watches behaviour, value types, usage-spec linting, env prefix collisions.",

# skogai <module> <cmd>...: run a module's argc command with its env (`skogai module env`);

core="$root/modules/core/argc.sh"

case "${1:-}" in
"" | -* | config | module | help) ;;
*)
    if cmd="$(argc --argc-run "$core" module command "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; then
        eval "$(argc --argc-run "$core" module env "$1")"
        shift
        exec argc --argc-run "$cmd" "$@"
    fi
    ;;
esac
exec argc --argc-run "$core" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai core: config across layers, and the modules skogai is made of
#
# a module is a directory with a module.md: frontmatter says what it is, which
# argc script is its command, which files it offers and its config defaults.
# modules are found installed (local .skogai/modules, then global), then in
# the sources on $SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH. the first one by a name wins.
# @meta require-tools git,yq
# @meta binname skogai
# @env SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR=/etc/skogai  dir of the system layer config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR  dir of the global layer, default ~/.config/skogai
# @env SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR=.skogai  dir of the local layer; relative is from the git root, or pwd
# @env SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH  colon-separated dirs of module sources, default the one this module sits in

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

SELF="$(realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
GLOBAL_DIR="${SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/skogai}"
MODULE_PATH="${SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH:-$(dirname "$(dirname "$SELF")")}"

# joins the items of a list value; `get` prints one item per line
SEP=$'\x1f'

# @cmd read and write key/value config across system, global, local and module layers
#
# fold order, later wins: module.md `config:` defaults, system, global, local,
# module.local.md overrides, --file layers, then SKOGAI_* env.
# a module's keys are mounted under its name: runner's `model` is `runner.model`.
config() { :; }

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key![`_choice_key`]
config::get() {
    local line
    line="$(_line "$argc_key")" || exit $?
    if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
    else
        cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
    fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  write this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![?`_choice_key`]
# @arg value!
config::set() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")" && printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"; }
        K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
    git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  remove from this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![`_choice_target_key`]
config::unset() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
        K="$key" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::list() {
    local key value origin item resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
            if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
                printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
            else
                printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
            fi
        done <<<"$value$SEP"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::env() {
    local key value origin resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
config::files() {
    local layer file name dir

# @cmd the env a module's command runs with, as export lines
#
# SKOGAI_MODULE, SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR, SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR and SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR
# (both absolute), and the module's own resolved keys: runner.model is
# SKOGAI_RUNNER_MODEL.
# @arg name![`_choice_module`]
module::env() {
    local dir key value
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1
    printf 'export SKOGAI_MODULE=%q\n' "$argc_name"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR=%q\n' "$dir"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR=%q\n' "$(_local_dir)"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR=%q\n' "$GLOBAL_DIR"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value _; do
        [[ $key == "$argc_name".* ]] || continue
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done < <(_resolve)
}

# @cmd copy a module into .skogai/modules, or the global dir. prints the plan unless --apply
#
# copies module.md, its command and its `files:`. a file already there and
# different is kept and reported; `skogai module diff` shows how.
# exit 1 when there is something to copy and --apply was not given.
# @arg source![?`_choice_source`]  a module name from the sources, or a path to a module dir
# @option --to[local|global]  where to install, default core.module.install
# @flag --apply  copy the files
module::add() {
    local src name to dest rel status todo=0
    src="$(_source "$argc_source")" || { echo "no module source: $argc_source" >&2; exit 2; }
    name="$(basename "$src")"
    to="${argc_to:-$(_get core.module.install local)}"
    dest="$(_install_dir "$to")/$name"
    [[ $src != "$dest" ]] || { echo "already installed: $dest" >&2; exit 0; }
    echo "$name: $src -> $dest" >&2
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
        if [[ ! -e $dest/$rel ]]; then
            status=add todo=1
        elif cmp -s "$src/$rel" "$dest/$rel"; then
            status=same
        else
            status=keep
        fi
        printf '%-5s %s\n' "$status" "$rel"
        if [[ $status == add && ${argc_apply:-} == 1 ]]; then
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$rel")"
            cp -p "$src/$rel" "$dest/$rel"
        fi
    done < <(_module_files "$src")
    _missing "$src" >&2
    [[ $todo == 0 || ${argc_apply:-} == 1 ]] || exit 1
}

# @cmd diff an installed module against its source
# @arg name![`_choice_installed`]
module::diff() {
    local dir src rel rc=0
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1
    src="$(_source "$argc_name")" || { echo "no source for $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
        diff -u --label "source/$rel" --label "installed/$rel" "$src/$rel" "$dir/$rel" 2>/dev/null || rc=1
    done < <(_module_files "$src")
    return "$rc"
}

# @cmd scaffold a new module from core's templates/module
# @arg name!  lowercase, one segment
# @arg description  what it is, one line
# @option --to[local|global]  where to create it, default core.module.install
module::new() {
    [[ $argc_name =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "bad name: $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    ! _reserved "$argc_name" || { echo "reserved: $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    local to dest core tpl f
    to="${argc_to:-$(_get core.module.install local)}"
    dest="$(_install_dir "$to")/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e $dest ]] || { echo "exists: $dest" >&2; exit 2; }
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ core < <(_module core)
    tpl="$core/templates/module"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$f")"
        NAME="$argc_name" DESC="${argc_description:-}" \
            awk '{ gsub(/\{\{name\}\}/, ENVIRON["NAME"]); gsub(/\{\{description\}\}/, ENVIRON["DESC"]); gsub(/\{\{NAME\}\}/, toupper(ENVIRON["NAME"])); print }' \
            "$tpl/$f" >"$dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}"
        [[ ! -x $tpl/$f ]] || chmod +x "$dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}"
        echo "wrote $dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}" >&2
    done < <(cd "$tpl" && find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | sort)
}

# the resolved "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" line of a key; exit 1 if unset
_line() {
    local resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || return 2
    awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k { print; f = 1 } END { exit !f }' <<<"$resolved"
}

# a resolved value, or $2 if unset
_get() { _line "$1" | cut -f2 | grep . || echo "${2:-}"; }

_local_dir() {
    local dir="${SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR:-.skogai}"
    [[ $dir == /* ]] || dir="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)/$dir"
    echo "$dir"
}

_install_dir() {
    case "$1" in
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/modules" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/modules" ;;
    *) echo "bad --to: $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
}

_present() { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$([[ -f $2 ]] && echo present || echo missing)"; }

# layers in fold order, later wins: system, global, local
_layer_file() {
    case "$1" in
    system) echo "$SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/config" ;;
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/config" ;;
    esac
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# a module's overrides: beside its module.md when installed; a source one's
# go in the local install dir, never into the source
_module_local_md() {
    if [[ $2 == source ]]; then echo "$(_install_dir local)/$1/module.local.md"; else echo "$3/module.local.md"; fi
}

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
        echo "$f"
        _local_md "$f"
    done
}

# set/unset into a markdown file: sets `file`, and `argc_scope` for --module
_md_target() {
    if [[ -n ${argc_module:-} ]]; then
        local layer dir
        IFS=$'\t' read -r _ layer dir < <(_module "$argc_module") || { echo "no module: $argc_module" >&2; exit 2; }
        file="$(_module_local_md "$argc_module" "$layer" "$dir")"
        argc_scope="$argc_module"
        MD_ROOT=config
        return 0
    fi
    [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]] || return 1
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under the scope ($2, or --scope) if given, with `_` read as `-`.
# $3 picks the map to read, default the whole frontmatter. a list is one value,
# its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    yq --front-matter=extract "select(document_index == 0) | ${3:-.} // {}" "$1" |
        SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${2-${argc_scope:-}}" yq '
        select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")'
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag name dir fm entry
    _fold() { # file scope root origin
        [[ -f $1 ]] || return 0
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$1" "$2" "$3")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                builtin unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="$4"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    }
    local mods
    mods="$(_modules)"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$dir/module.md" "$name" .config "module:$name"
    done <<<"$mods"
    for layer in system global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")" "$name" .config "module:$name.local"
    done <<<"$mods"
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _fold "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" . "file:$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# every resolved key, only --module's own if given; choices for get and set,
# described by value when completing
_choice_key() {
    local keys
    keys="$(_resolve | awk -F'\t' -v m="${argc_module:-}" 'm == "" || index($1, m ".") == 1')"
    if [[ ${ARGC_COMPGEN:-0} == 1 ]]; then cut -f1,2 <<<"$keys" | tr "$SEP" ' '; else cut -f1 <<<"$keys"; fi
}

# keys present in the layer set/unset write to; choices for unset
_choice_target_key() {
    local file
    if _md_target 2>/dev/null; then
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then _frontmatter "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" "${MD_ROOT:+.$MD_ROOT}" | cut -f1; fi
    else
        file="$(_target_file)"
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then git config -f "$file" --name-only --list; fi
    fi
}

_choice_module() { _modules | cut -f1; }
_choice_installed() { _modules | awk -F'\t' '$2 != "source" { print $1 }'; }
_choice_source() { _module_bases | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "source" { print $2 }' | while read -r p; do ls "$p"; done | sort -u; }

# the frontmatter path of a key in a markdown layer: the key minus its scope,
# under `config.` for a module's module.local.md
_file_key() {
    local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
    if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
        [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || { echo "key $key is outside $scope" >&2; return 2; }
        key="${key#"$scope".}"
    fi
    [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad key: $1" >&2; return 2; }
    echo "${MD_ROOT:+$MD_ROOT.}$key"
}

tool_input.content:
Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers").

Precedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):
- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.
- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.
- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.
- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.
- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = "{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. tool_input.content:
Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory; outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall and skipped by ls.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` whose `_.skogai` is a table with at least one key (yq -p toml); every other file there (e.g. the host's own conf.d files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T the source toml and the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level, except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace. Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call. The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); a module with the same name already installed at another level is rejected (duplicate-name); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons, sorted unique, or ["tests-failed"]), exit 1, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: target <conf.d>/<name>.toml. Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 1, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local, files sorted (C locale) within a level. No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent), 1 rejected, 2 bad args, bad path, target conflict, local level outside git, or a missing tool (yq, jq, and bats when tests exist). Diagnostics on stderr only.

Docs: new docs/install.md: levels and directories, what counts as a module file, the checks and their order, the output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: same-named modules at two levels are refused rather than shadowed; owns paths of installed modules are compared relative to their conf.d; module tests run unisolated in the module's directory.

- local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory; outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall and skipped by ls.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` whose `_.skogai` is a table with at least one key (yq -p toml); every other file there (e.g. the host's own conf.d files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T the source toml and the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level, except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace. Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call. The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); a module with the same name already installed at another level is rejected (duplicate-name); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons, sorted unique, or ["tests-failed"]), exit 1, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: target <conf.d>/<name>.toml. Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 1, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local, files sorted (C locale) within a level. No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent), 1 rejected, 2 bad args, bad path, target conflict, local level outside git, or a missing tool (yq, jq, and bats when tests exist). Diagnostics on stderr only.

Docs: new docs/install.md: levels and directories, what counts as a module file, the checks and their order, the output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: same-named modules at two levels are refused rather than shadowed; owns paths of installed modules are compared relative to their conf.d; module tests run unisolated in the module's directory.

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/install.bats with fixtures under tests/fixtures/install/ (module directories and toml files of its own; it must not modify examples/). Every test isolates HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR and uses a `git init` project dir. Required cases: install to each level puts the file in the right conf.d and prints the exact JSON; a second install is `unchanged` with the file's mtime unchanged; a changed source gives `updated`; an invalid module (one F003 reason fixture) is rejected with that reason and nothing is written; missing-dependency rejected, then accepted after the dependency is installed at a broader level; duplicate-name across levels rejected; ownership-conflict with an installed module rejected; a module directory whose bats test fails is rejected with tests-failed, and one whose test passes is installed; a foreign non-module file at the target name gives exit 2 and is untouched; foreign files in conf.d are ignored by ls and by the rules; uninstall removes, then reports absent; uninstall refused while another installed module depends on it; local level outside a git dir is exit 2; live: after `install --level global` of a fixture module with a task, `mise run -q <task>` (isolated mise as in tests/module.bats, from the project dir) runs it, and after uninstall the task is gone (mise exits non-zero). Reached through a registry symlink it still works. `mise run test`, `mise run test:argc` and `.harness/init.sh smoke_test` pass.

Out of scope: config get/set (F004), run executing a module with its env (D), depends_on checked at run time (E), install from a URL or git, scaffolding (`module new`), `module diff`, copying files beside the toml.",

      "description": "Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary \"Module model and config answers\").\n\nPrecedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):\n- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = \"{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}\"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.\n- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.\n- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.\n- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.\n- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.\n- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = \"{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}\"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).\n\nKeys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.\n\nCommands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case \"$usage_cmd\"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):\n- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 1 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else a module toml in a conf.d that defines it, printed `module:<name>` (name = its single `_.skogai` key; project conf.d before global before system); else `mise` (some other mise file defines it).\n- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json`, sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0.\n- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Every other line of the file (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept. Values containing `'`, `\\`, a newline, or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed.\n- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env]; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.\n- `files`: one `<layer>\\t<path>\\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\\t<path>\\tpresent` line per module toml found in system conf.d, global conf.d, project .mise/conf.d and .config/mise/conf.d (in that order, files sorted). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`.\nOutside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Bad args: exit 2. Diagnostics go to stderr only.\n\nModule defaults: change examples/modules/hello/hello.toml to `SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = \"{{ env.SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING | default(value='hi') }}\"` and say in docs/module.md that module defaults use this form and why (a get_env default in a later layer beats earlier settings). The checker does not enforce the form in this feature. tests/module.bats must stay green unchanged (its live test still prints `hi world` / `yo world`).\n\nDocs: new docs/config.md: the layers and files, the key mapping, the stored form, every command with output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: the reverse mapping loses `-`; a shell with `mise activate` exports resolved SKOGAI_* values, so they show as origin `env`; values with the refused characters cannot be stored (types are deferred).\n\nEvidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/config.bats. Every test isolates mise like tests/module.bats: `env -i PATH HOME` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR, MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, XDG_STATE_HOME isolated, and a `git init` project dir. Required cases:\n1. Precedence ladder: hello.toml copied into the project's .mise/conf.d; then step by step: nothing set -> `get --show-origin hello.greeting` = `module:hello\\thi`; `set --system` sys -> system; `set --global` glob -> global; `set` loc -> local; `set --override` ovr -> override; caller env SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING=env -> `env`. At every step `mise run -q hello world` from the project prints `<that value> world` (the task sees what get reports).\n2. A global setting beats a module installed in the project conf.d (the env.K default form).\n3. set keeps a comment and a [tools] table already in mise.toml; set twice leaves one entry; unset removes it and a second unset is exit 0.\n4. Refused values (each of the listed characters) exit 2 and leave the file byte-identical.\n5. Invalid keys (`Hello`, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `1a`, empty) exit 2.\n6. get of an unset key: exit 1, empty stdout.\n7. list output exact for a known setup, with and without --show-origin.\n8. files output exact inside a git dir and outside one.\n9. Reached through a registry symlink (`skogai register`) it still works.\n`mise run test`, `mise run test:argc` and `.harness/init.sh smoke_test` pass.\n\nOut of scope: install/uninstall (F005), run injecting module env into Podman (D), command parameters as a layer, typed values, mise.<env>.toml (MISE_ENV) layers, config.override.toml, `--file` layers from best-version, completion of keys.",

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions

  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.

A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Layer merge (same session): `[env]` merges key by key and the later layer wins; a later `[tasks.x]` replaces the whole task, so `run` and `usage` vanish silently; `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file. An empty .toml parses to `null` in yq. A test can isolate mise with `env -i` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS: then `/etc/mise/conf.d` is not loaded. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. ### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.

# Module format v1

A module's declaration is a mise config file, and the contract checker reads it. Decided with skogix 2026-11-07 (see `.harness/context_summary.md`, "Module model and config answers" and "mise conf.d").

Status words: **implemented** means the code does it; **verified** means a test in `tests/module.bats` covers it; **by hand** means someone ran it once and no test covers it; **planned** is not built.

## Layout (convention, not checked)

The checker only receives files, so layout is documentation. In source a module is a directory `<name>/`:

- `<name>.toml`: a mise config file. Later installed as a conf.d drop-in, so the file name is the module name.
- `README.md`: what the module is, every key it sets, what it owns.
- `SKOGAI.md` (optional): agent-facing entry.
- `tests/` (optional).

The example is [examples/modules/hello/](../examples/modules/hello/).

## The declaration

A module is three things in one file: key/value defaults (`[env]`), a usage declaration (the task's `usage`), and relationships (`_.skogai.<name>`).

```toml
[env]
SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = "{{ get_env(name='SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING', default='hi') }}"

[_.skogai.hello]
description = "..."
owns = ["greeting.txt"]
writes = ["greeting.txt"]

[tasks.hello]
usage = 'arg "<who>"'
run = 'echo "$SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING $usage_who" | tee greeting.txt'
```

- **Name**: the single key under `_.skogai`. It is the name used in the data record, the env prefix, task names and every cross-file rule. The file stem is compared with it only for `name-mismatch`.
- **Which files are modules**: a case-sensitive `.toml` suffix with a non-empty stem. Everything else (`.TOML`, `.toml` alone, `x.toml.md`) is parsed as Markdown, as before.
- **Top-level keys**: `_`, `env`, `tasks`. Under `_` only `skogai`.
- **Relationship keys** in `_.skogai.<name>`: `description`, `depends_on`, `reads`, `writes`, `owns`, `watches`. Type and path rules are the Markdown ones (see `docs/runner.md` and F001). `name` and `defaults` are not allowed (the name is the table key, defaults are `[env]`). `watches` has no behaviour yet (planned).
- **`[env]`** is optional and must be a table. Every key except mise's directive key `_` must start with `SKOGAI_<N>_` and be longer than it, where `<N>` is the name uppercased with `-` removed. Values are not checked (types are deferred).
- **Tasks**: `tasks.<name>` is required, a table with a string `usage` and `run` (string or array of strings). Other tasks must be `<name>:<sub>`, `<sub>` matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. The usage string is not linted.

Implemented and verified: the checker output is the same `{file, verdict, reasons}` per file, reasons sorted and unique, exit codes unchanged. Markdown output is byte-identical to before. Only `src/core/contract/usage.sh` reads modules; the frozen `argc.sh` does not.

## Reasons

Parse stage. Exactly one reason, nothing else is checked, and the file takes no part in cross-file rules:

| reason | when |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid-toml` | `yq -p toml -o json` exits non-zero |
| `no-declaration` | document is empty or not a table, `_` is missing or not a table, or `_.skogai` is missing, not a table, or empty |
| `multiple-declarations` | `_.skogai` has more than one key, even if one equals the stem |
| `not-a-mapping` | the value of the single `_.skogai.<name>` key is not a table (an empty table is valid) |

Collected reasons (any number, with the shared field reasons, then the cross-file ones):

| reason | when |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid-name` | name does not match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` (shared rule) |
| `name-mismatch` | name differs from the file stem; `hello.toml` with key `Hello` gets both |
| `unknown-key` | key in the relationship table other than the six allowed |
| `env-outside-prefix` | an `[env]` key outside `SKOGAI_<N>_`, or the bare prefix alone |
| `missing-task` | no `tasks.<name>` table with a string `usage` and a `run` |
| `task-outside-prefix` | a task other than `<name>` or `<name>:<sub>` |
| `unknown-section` | a top-level key other than `_ env tasks`, or a key other than `skogai` under `_` |
| `wrong-type` | shared rule; also `env` present but not a table |

The shared cross-file reasons (`missing-dependency`, `duplicate-name`, `ownership-conflict`, `write-not-owned`, `path-outside-scope`) apply to `.md` and `.toml` files together; a workorder and a module that own the same path conflict. An invalid name still takes part in the cross-file rules, as in F001.

Verified by the fixtures in `tests/fixtures/module/` (`valid/`, `invalid/<reason>/`), kept apart from `tests/fixtures/contract/` because `mise run test:argc` runs `contract.bats` against the frozen argc checker.

## Open

- Two modules whose prefixes collide (`a-b` and `ab` both give `SKOGAI_AB_`) are not detected.
- A TOML construct that mise accepts but yq rejects or decodes differently is judged by what yq yields.
- Value types, usage-spec linting, install, config get/set, run executing the task, `depends_on` at run time and `watches` behaviour are planned, not built.

## mise facts (mise 2026.10.17, verified by hand on 2026-11-07, not by a test)

- conf.d is loaded at system (`/etc/mise/conf.d`), global (`~/.config/mise/conf.d`, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`) and project level (`.mise/conf.d`, `.config/mise/conf.d`).
- `[env]` merges key by key across layers, a later layer winning.
- A later layer's `[tasks.x]` replaces the whole task. So only the module's own file defines its tasks and relationships; override files set `[env]` only.
- `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file, no merge.
- A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env; a `get_env` default does not.

The one thing a test does cover (verified, in `tests/module.bats`): copying `hello.toml` into a project's `.mise/conf.d/` and running `mise run -q hello world` under an isolated mise (`env -i`, every `MISE_*` dir under the test's tmp dir, `MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS`) prints `hi world`, writes `greeting.txt`, and prints `yo world` when the caller sets `SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING=yo`.

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Layer merge (same session): `[env]` merges key by key and the later layer wins; a later `[tasks.x]` replaces the whole task, so `run` and `usage` vanish silently; `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file. An empty .toml parses to `null` in yq. A test can isolate mise with `env -i` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS: then `/etc/mise/conf.d` is not loaded. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.

## Meta-Patterns
<!-- Coordination insights that apply across features — NOT domain-specific.
     Populated by the retrospective step at session end. -->
- (none yet — first retrospective will populate this)

## Meta-Session 2026-10-29
- Scope accuracy: no features yet; session covered scaffolding and the foundation-first plan (docs/plan.md, AGENTS.md).
- Model calibration: n/a, no agents spawned.
- Discovery lineage: n/a.
- Approach patterns: harness ceremony (improve loop, spec gate) was explained at length before any feature existed; skogix asked for the simple path. Prefer acting on bookkeeping over describing it.
- Plan approval: n/a.

## Meta-Session 2026-11-06
