# @cmd read and write key/value config across system, global, local and module layers
#
# fold order, later wins: module.md `config:` defaults, system, global, local,
# module.local.md overrides, --file layers, then SKOGAI_* env.
# a module's keys are mounted under its name: runner's `model` is `runner.model`.
config() { :; }

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key![`_choice_key`]
config::get() {
    local line
    line="$(_line "$argc_key")" || exit $?
    if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
    else
        cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
    fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  write this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![?`_choice_key`]
# @arg value!
config::set() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")" && printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"; }
        K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
    git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  remove from this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![`_choice_target_key`]
config::unset() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
        K="$key" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::list() {
    local key value origin item resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
            if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
                printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
            else
                printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
            fi
        done <<<"$value$SEP"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::env() {
    local key value origin resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
config::files() {
    local layer file name dir
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        _present "module:$name" "$dir/module.md"
    done < <(_modules)
    for layer in system global local; do
        _present "$layer" "$(_layer_file "$layer")"
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        _present "module:$name" "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")"
    done < <(_modules)
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _present file "$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
}

_present() { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$([[ -f $2 ]] && echo present || echo missing)"; }

# layers in fold order, later wins: system, global, local
_layer_file() {
    case "$1" in
    system) echo "$SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/config" ;;
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/config" ;;
    esac
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# a module's overrides: beside its module.md when installed; a source one's
# go in the local install dir, never into the source
_module_local_md() {
    if [[ $2 == source ]]; then echo "$(_install_dir local)/$1/module.local.md"; else echo "$3/module.local.md"; fi
}

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
        echo "$f"
        _local_md "$f"
    done
}

# set/unset into a markdown file: sets `file`, and `argc_scope` for --module
_md_target() {
    if [[ -n ${argc_module:-} ]]; then
        local layer dir
        IFS=$'\t' read -r _ layer dir < <(_module "$argc_module") || { echo "no module: $argc_module" >&2; exit 2; }
        file="$(_module_local_md "$argc_module" "$layer" "$dir")"
        argc_scope="$argc_module"
        MD_ROOT=config
        return 0
    fi
    [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]] || return 1
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under the scope ($2, or --scope) if given, with `_` read as `-`.
# $3 picks the map to read, default the whole frontmatter. a list is one value,
# its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    yq --front-matter=extract "select(document_index == 0) | ${3:-.} // {}" "$1" |
        SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${2-${argc_scope:-}}" yq '
        select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")'
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag name dir fm entry
    _fold() { # file scope root origin
        [[ -f $1 ]] || return 0
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$1" "$2" "$3")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                builtin unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="$4"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    }
    local mods
    mods="$(_modules)"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$dir/module.md" "$name" .config "module:$name"
    done <<<"$mods"
    for layer in system global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")" "$name" .config "module:$name.local"
    done <<<"$mods"
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _fold "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" . "file:$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# every resolved key, only --module's own if given; choices for get and set,
# described by value when completing
_choice_key() {
    local keys
    keys="$(_resolve | awk -F'\t' -v m="${argc_module:-}" 'm == "" || index($1, m ".") == 1')"
    if [[ ${ARGC_COMPGEN:-0} == 1 ]]; then cut -f1,2 <<<"$keys" | tr "$SEP" ' '; else cut -f1 <<<"$keys"; fi
}

# keys present in the layer set/unset write to; choices for unset
_choice_target_key() {
    local file
    if _md_target 2>/dev/null; then
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then _frontmatter "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" "${MD_ROOT:+.$MD_ROOT}" | cut -f1; fi
    else
        file="$(_target_file)"
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then git config -f "$file" --name-only --list; fi
    fi
}

_choice_module() { _modules | cut -f1; }
_choice_installed() { _modules | awk -F'\t' '$2 != "source" { print $1 }'; }
_choice_source() { _module_bases | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "source" { print $2 }' | while read -r p; do ls "$p"; done | sort -u; }

# the frontmatter path of a key in a markdown layer: the key minus its scope,
# under `config.` for a module's module.local.md
_file_key() {
    local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
    if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
        [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || { echo "key $key is outside $scope" >&2; return 2; }
        key="${key#"$scope".}"
    fi
    [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad key: $1" >&2; return 2; }
    echo "${MD_ROOT:+$MD_ROOT.}$key"
}

check() {
    local tool file version files=()

Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory; outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall and skipped by ls.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` whose `_.skogai` is a table with at least one key (yq -p toml); every other file there (e.g. the host's own conf.d files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T the source toml and the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level, except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace. Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call. The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); a module with the same name already installed at another level is rejected (duplicate-name); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons, sorted unique, or ["tests-failed"]), exit 1, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: target <conf.d>/<name>.toml. Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 1, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local, files sorted (C locale) within a level. No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent), 1 rejected, 2 bad args, bad path, target conflict, local level outside git, or a missing tool (yq, jq, and bats when tests exist). Diagnostics on stderr only.

Docs: new docs/install.md: levels and directories, what counts as a module file, the checks and their order, the output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: same-named modules at two levels are refused rather than shadowed; owns paths of installed modules are compared relative to their conf.d; module tests run unisolated in the module's directory.

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/install.bats with fixtures under tests/fixtures/install/ (module directories and toml files of its own; it must not modify examples/). Every test isolates HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR and uses a `git init` project dir. Required cases: install to each level puts the file in the right conf.d and prints the exact JSON; a second install is `unchanged` with the file's mtime unchanged; a changed source gives `updated`; an invalid module (one F003 reason fixture) is rejected with that reason and nothing is written; missing-dependency rejected, then accepted after the dependency is installed at a broader level; duplicate-name across levels rejected; ownership-conflict with an installed module rejected; a module directory whose bats test fails is rejected with tests-failed, and one whose test passes is installed; a foreign non-module file at the target name gives exit 2 and is untouched; foreign files in conf.d are ignored by ls and by the rules; uninstall removes, then reports absent; uninstall refused while another installed module depends on it; local level outside a git dir is exit 2; live: after `install --level global` of a fixture module with a task, `mise run -q <task>` (isolated mise as in tests/module.bats, from the project dir) runs it, and after uninstall the task is gone (mise exits non-zero). Reached through a registry symlink it still works. `mise run test`, `mise run test:argc` and `.harness/init.sh smoke_test` pass.

Out of scope: config get/set (F004), run executing a module with its env (D), depends_on checked at run time (E), install from a URL or git, scaffolding (`module new`), `module diff`, copying files beside the toml.

Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers").

Precedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):
- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.
- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.
- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.
- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.
- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = "{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 1 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else a module toml in a conf.d that defines it, printed `module:<name>` (name = its single `_.skogai` key; project conf.d before global before system); else `mise` (some other mise file defines it).
- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json`, sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0.
- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Every other line of the file (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept. Values containing `'`, `\`, a newline, or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed.
- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env]; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.
- `files`: one `<layer>\t<path>\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\t<path>\tpresent` line per module toml found in system conf.d, global conf.d, project .mise/conf.d and .config/mise/conf.d (in that order, files sorted). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`.
Outside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Bad args: exit 2. Diagnostics go to stderr only.

Module defaults: change examples/modules/hello/hello.toml to `SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = "{{ env.SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING | default(value='hi') }}"` and say in docs/module.md that module defaults use this form and why (a get_env default in a later layer beats earlier settings). The checker does not enforce the form in this feature. tests/module.bats must stay green unchanged (its live test still prints `hi world` / `yo world`).

The conf.d directories, in mise's load order (broadest first): `$SYS/conf.d`, `$CFG/conf.d`, `<git root>/.mise/conf.d`, `<git root>/.config/mise/conf.d`; files within one directory in C-locale order. Outside a git work tree the two project directories are not read.

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 1 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else a module toml in a conf.d that defines it, printed `module:<name>` (name = its single `_.skogai` key; project conf.d before global before system); else `mise` (some other mise file defines it).
- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json`, sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0.
- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Every other line of the file (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept. Values containing `'`, `\`, a newline, or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed.
- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env]; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.
- `files`: one `<layer>\t<path>\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\t<path>\tpresent` line per module toml found in system conf.d, global conf.d, project .mise/conf.d and .config/mise/conf.d (in that order, files sorted). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`.
Outside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Bad args: exit 2. Diagnostics go to stderr only.

Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: install and uninstall write <git root>/.mise/conf.d; reading (ls, rules, the duplicate-name scan, required-by) covers both <git root>/.mise/conf.d and <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d (mise loads both), in that order. git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory. Outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall, and it is simply left out of ls, the rules set, the duplicate-name scan and required-by.
Paths (the JSON `path` field, the conf.d directories) are built literally from those variables and the git root, not passed through realpath.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` that yq parses, whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is the module's name. Every other file there (the host's own conf.d files, files with several `_.skogai` keys, unparseable files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T, flat, under their own file names: first the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level (broadest level first; a later file with the same file name replaces an earlier one), except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace; then the source toml under its own file name (replacing any copy of the same file name). Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call (C-locale sorted). The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
1b. Duplicate name at any level: if the source is valid, and a skogai module file declaring the same name is installed at any level (narrower ones included) other than the target file <conf.d>/<name>.toml itself, the install is rejected with reason `duplicate-name`. This scan is separate from the checker so that narrower levels do not satisfy missing-dependency.
If contract/usage.sh exits non-zero or its output is not one JSON verdict per file, install exits 2 with its stderr passed through, nothing on stdout, nothing written.
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons sorted unique, or ["duplicate-name"], or ["tests-failed"]), exit 3, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr. If creating the directory, copying or renaming fails (e.g. no permission at the system level): exit 4, a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, and the temporary file is removed.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: <name> must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, else exit 2. Target <conf.d>/<name>.toml (for local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d only). Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 3, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0. If removing fails: exit 4, message on stderr, nothing on stdout.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local, files sorted (C locale) within a level. No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent); 1 only from usage's own parser (a command line that does not fit the #USAGE spec, as in run/usage.sh); 2 bad args, bad path or name, target conflict, local level outside git, checker failure, or a missing tool (git, yq, jq, and bats when tests exist); 3 rejected; 4 the effect failed. Diagnostics on stderr only.

      "description": "Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers").

Precedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):
- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.
- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.
- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.
- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.
- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = "{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).

Module files: a "skogai module file" is a `*.toml` in one of the conf.d directories below that yq parses and whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is its name (the same definition as F005). Every other file there is ignored. The conf.d directories, in mise's load order (broadest first): `$SYS/conf.d`, `$CFG/conf.d`, `<git root>/.mise/conf.d`, `<git root>/.config/mise/conf.d`; files within one directory in C-locale order. Outside a git work tree the two project directories are not read.

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 3 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else the first module file in load order (broadest first, as above: with the env.K default form the earliest-loaded default wins) whose [env] has it, printed `module:<name>`; else `mise`. Origin is skogai's ladder, not mise's internal record: a value supplied by a file outside the ladder (a subdirectory mise.toml, `.mise.toml`, `.config/mise.toml`, config.override.toml, a module default not in the env.K form) can be attributed to a ladder file that also defines it. That is a documented known limit.
- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json` whose reverse key is a valid key (others, e.g. SKOGAI_A__B, are skipped), sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0. In list output and in `get --show-origin` output, a value is printed with `\` as `\\`, newline as `\n` and tab as `\t`; plain `get` prints the raw value.
- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Values containing `'`, `"`, `\`, any control character (newline, tab, CR, ...), or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed. An existing target file that yq cannot parse as TOML: exit 2, untouched. The write is atomic: copy the target (or an empty file) to a temporary file in the same directory whose name mise does not load (e.g. `.skogai-set-XXXXXX.toml`), edit that copy (preferably with `mise set --file` / `mise unset --file`, trusting mise's TOML editing), then rename it over the target; on failure the temporary file is removed and the target untouched, exit 2. Contract tested on the standard form (`K = "..."` lines under an `[env]` header): every other line (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept, and a second set leaves one entry. For other forms (inline `env = {...}`, dotted `env.K`, duplicates) the outcome is whatever the mise edit does, provided `mise env` then resolves the new value; docs say so.
- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env], same atomic write; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.
- `files`: one `<layer>\t<path>\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\t<path>\tpresent` line per module file in load order (see Module files). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`, and no project module lines are printed.
Outside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing git, mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 only from usage's own parser (missing <key>, unknown flag; contract/usage.sh records this); 2 bad args, refused value, tool or mise failure; 3 get of an undefined key. Diagnostics go to stderr only.

Every test isolates mise like tests/module.bats: `env -i PATH HOME` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR, MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, XDG_STATE_HOME isolated, and a `git init` project dir. Required cases:
1. Precedence ladder: hello.toml copied into the project's .mise/conf.d; then step by step: nothing set -> `get --show-origin hello.greeting` = `module:hello\thi`; `set --system` sys -> system; `set --global` glob -> global; `set` loc -> local; `set --override` ovr -> override; caller env SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING=env -> `env`. 3. set keeps a comment and a [tools] table already in mise.toml; set twice leaves one entry; unset removes it and a second unset is exit 0.

8. files output exact inside a git dir and outside one, with a host-style non-module file in a conf.d (not listed).
9. Through the registry: `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config` into a temporary SKOGAI_COMMANDS (SKOGAI_MAIN pointing at src/core/main-usage.sh, as tests/main-usage.bats does), then `skogai config set --global hello.greeting x` exits 0 and `skogai config get --show-origin hello.greeting` prints exactly `global\tx`.

"description": "Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: install and uninstall write <git root>/.mise/conf.d; reading (ls, rules, the duplicate-name scan, required-by) covers both <git root>/.mise/conf.d and <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d (mise loads both), in that order. git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory. Outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall, and it is simply left out of ls, the rules set, the duplicate-name scan and required-by.
Paths (the JSON `path` field, the conf.d directories) are built literally from those variables and the git root, not passed through realpath.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` that yq parses, whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is the module's name. Every other file there (the host's own conf.d files, files with several `_.skogai` keys, unparseable files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T, flat, under their own file names: first the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level (broadest level first; a later file with the same file name replaces an earlier one), except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace; then the source toml under its own file name (replacing any copy of the same file name). Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call (C-locale sorted). The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
1b. Duplicate name at any level: if the source is valid, and a skogai module file declaring the same name is installed at any level (narrower ones included) other than the target file <conf.d>/<name>.toml itself, the install is rejected with reason `duplicate-name`. This scan is separate from the checker so that narrower levels do not satisfy missing-dependency.
If contract/usage.sh exits non-zero or its output is not one JSON verdict per file, install exits 2 with its stderr passed through, nothing on stdout, nothing written.
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons sorted unique, or ["duplicate-name"], or ["tests-failed"]), exit 3, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr. If creating the directory, copying or renaming fails (e.g. no permission at the system level): exit 4, a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, and the temporary file is removed.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: <name> must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, else exit 2. Target <conf.d>/<name>.toml (for local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d only). Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 3, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0. If removing fails: exit 4, message on stderr, nothing on stdout.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local, files sorted (C locale) within a level. No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent); 1 only from usage's own parser (a command line that does not fit the #USAGE spec, as in run/usage.sh); 2 bad args, bad path or name, target conflict, local level outside git, checker failure, or a missing tool (git, yq, jq, and bats when tests exist); 3 rejected; 4 the effect failed. Diagnostics on stderr only.

Docs: new docs/install.md: levels and directories, what counts as a module file, the checks and their order, the output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: same-named modules at two levels are refused rather than shadowed; owns paths of installed modules are compared relative to their conf.d; module tests run unisolated in the module's directory.

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/install.bats with fixtures under tests/fixtures/install/ (module directories and toml files of its own; it must not modify examples/). Every test isolates HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR and uses a `git init` project dir. Required cases: install to each level puts the file in the right conf.d and prints the exact JSON; a second install is `unchanged` with the file's mtime unchanged; a changed source gives `updated`; an invalid module (one F003 reason fixture) is rejected with that reason and nothing is written; missing-dependency rejected, then accepted after the dependency is installed at a broader level; duplicate-name rejected both when the same name sits at a broader level and at a narrower one (e.g. installed local, installing global); a missing-dependency is not satisfied by a module at a narrower level; uninstall of an invalid name (`../x`) exit 2; a module in <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d shows in ls as level local; a read-only conf.d directory gives exit 4 with no temporary file left; ownership-conflict with an installed module rejected; a module directory whose bats test fails is rejected with tests-failed, and one whose test passes is installed; a foreign non-module file at the target name gives exit 2 and is untouched; foreign files in conf.d are ignored by ls and by the rules; uninstall removes, then reports absent; uninstall refused while another installed module depends on it; local level outside a git dir is exit 2; live: after `install --level global` of a fixture module with a task, `mise run -q <task>` (isolated mise as in tests/module.bats, from the project dir) runs it, and after uninstall the task is gone (mise exits non-zero). Tests that need mise skip when `mise` is not on PATH, as tests/module.bats does. `mise run test`, `mise run test:argc` and `.harness/init.sh smoke_test` pass.

Out of scope: config get/set (F004), run executing a module with its env (D), depends_on checked at run time (E), install from a URL or git, scaffolding (`module new`), `module diff`, copying files beside the toml.",

Both specs came back from the gate with questions: 17 for F004 (config) and 10 for F005 (install). They were all edge cases, so I answered them myself, amended both specs, and sent them back for a second pass. That's still running; once both pass, the two features can be built in parallel. Everything is uncommitted.

The answers that change what you'll see when you use these:
- **Exit codes:**

  | Code | F004 config | F005 install |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 | done | done |
  | 1 | malformed command line (usage's own error) | malformed command line |
  | 2 | bad arguments or tool failure | bad arguments or tool failure |
  | 3 | `get` of a key that isn't set | install refused by the module checks |
  | 4 | — | the file copy or removal itself failed |

  This means a key that isn't set gives 3, not git config's usual 1.
- **Duplicate names:** `module install` refuses a module whose name is already installed at any level, including a more local one (installing at global refuses if local already has it).
- **Writes:** `config set` replaces files atomically and refuses values containing quotes, backslashes, control characters, or the `{{` / `{%` / `{#` template markers.
- **Origin:** `config get --show-origin` only knows the files skogai manages. If a value comes from another mise file, such as a subdirectory's `mise.toml`, it can name the wrong layer. The docs list this as a known limit.

"description": "Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers").

Precedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):
- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.
- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.
- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.
- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.
- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = "{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).

Module files: a "skogai module file" is a `*.toml` in one of the conf.d directories below that yq parses and whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is its name (the same definition as F005). Every other file there is ignored. The conf.d directories, in mise's load order (broadest first): `$SYS/conf.d`, `$CFG/conf.d`, `<git root>/.mise/conf.d`, `<git root>/.config/mise/conf.d`; files within one directory in C-locale order. Outside a git work tree the two project directories are not read.

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 3 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else the first module file in load order (broadest first, as above: with the env.K default form the earliest-loaded default wins) whose [env] has it, printed `module:<name>`; else `mise`. Origin is skogai's ladder, not mise's internal record: a value supplied by a file outside the ladder (a subdirectory mise.toml, `.mise.toml`, `.config/mise.toml`, config.override.toml, a module default not in the env.K form) can be attributed to a ladder file that also defines it. That is a documented known limit.
- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json` whose reverse key is a valid key (others, e.g. SKOGAI_A__B, are skipped), sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0. In list output and in `get --show-origin` output, a value is printed with `\` as `\\`, newline as `\n` and tab as `\t`; plain `get` prints the raw value.
- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Values containing `'`, `"`, `\`, any control character (newline, tab, CR, ...), or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed. An existing target file that yq cannot parse as TOML: exit 2, untouched. The write is atomic: copy the target (or an empty file) to a temporary file in the same directory whose name mise does not load (e.g. `.skogai-set-XXXXXX.toml`), edit that copy (preferably with `mise set --file` / `mise unset --file`, trusting mise's TOML editing), then rename it over the target; on failure the temporary file is removed and the target untouched, exit 2. Contract tested on the standard form (`K = "..."` lines under an `[env]` header): every other line (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept, and a second set leaves one entry. For other forms (inline `env = {...}`, dotted `env.K`, duplicates) the outcome is whatever the mise edit does, provided `mise env` then resolves the new value; docs say so.
- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env], same atomic write; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.
- `files`: one `<layer>\t<path>\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\t<path>\tpresent` line per module file in load order (see Module files). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`, and no project module lines are printed.
Outside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing git, mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 only from usage's own parser (missing <key>, unknown flag; contract/usage.sh records this); 2 bad args, refused value, tool or mise failure; 3 get of an undefined key. Diagnostics go to stderr only.

Every test isolates mise like tests/module.bats: `env -i PATH HOME` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR, MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, XDG_STATE_HOME isolated, and a `git init` project dir. Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: install and uninstall write <git root>/.mise/conf.d; reading (ls, rules, the duplicate-name scan, required-by) covers both <git root>/.mise/conf.d and <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d (mise loads both), in that order. git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory. Outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall, and it is simply left out of ls, the rules set, the duplicate-name scan and required-by.
Paths (the JSON `path` field, the conf.d directories) are built literally from those variables and the git root, not passed through realpath.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` that yq parses, whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is the module's name. Every other file there (the host's own conf.d files, files with several `_.skogai` keys, unparseable files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T, flat, under their own file names: first the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level (broadest level first; a later file with the same file name replaces an earlier one), except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace; then the source toml under its own file name (replacing any copy of the same file name). Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call (C-locale sorted). The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
1b. Duplicate name at any level: if the source is valid, and a skogai module file declaring the same name is installed at any level (narrower ones included) other than the target file <conf.d>/<name>.toml itself, the install is rejected with reason `duplicate-name`. This scan is separate from the checker so that narrower levels do not satisfy missing-dependency.
If contract/usage.sh exits non-zero or its output is not one JSON verdict per file, install exits 2 with its stderr passed through, nothing on stdout, nothing written.
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons sorted unique, or ["duplicate-name"], or ["tests-failed"]), exit 3, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr. If creating the directory, copying or renaming fails (e.g. no permission at the system level): exit 4, a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, and the temporary file is removed.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: <name> must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, else exit 2. Target <conf.d>/<name>.toml (for local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d only). Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 3, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0. If removing fails: exit 4, message on stderr, nothing on stdout.

#!/usr/bin/env -S usage bash
#USAGE bin "module"
#USAGE about "install modules into the mise conf.d of a level by copying, and list them"
#USAGE long_about """
#USAGE a module is a mise config file (<name>.toml, see docs/module.md). `install` runs the contract checker over the module together with everything already installed at the target level and the broader ones, runs the module's bats tests when it is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory, and only then copies the toml into the conf.d of the level: system (${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d), global (the default, ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.config/mise}/conf.d) or local (<git root>/.mise/conf.d). see docs/install.md.
#USAGE
#USAGE stdout is JSON lines. exit 0 done (including unchanged and absent), 1 a command line that does not fit the spec (usage's own), 2 bad arguments, path or name, a conflicting target file, the local level outside a git work tree, a checker failure or a missing tool, 3 rejected, 4 the effect failed.
#USAGE """
#USAGE cmd "install" effect="write" help="validate a module, then copy its toml into a level's conf.d" {
#USAGE   flag "--level <level>" default="global" help="where to install" { choices "system" "global" "local" }
#USAGE   arg "<path>" help="a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <d>.toml (and optionally tests/)"
#USAGE }
#USAGE cmd "uninstall" effect="write" help="remove an installed module's toml from a level's conf.d" {
#USAGE   flag "--level <level>" default="global" help="where to remove from" { choices "system" "global" "local" }
#USAGE   arg "<name>" help="the module's name"
#USAGE }
#USAGE cmd "ls" effect="read" help="list the installed module files, system first, local last"
#
# usage parses the comments above and exports usage_cmd, usage_level, usage_path
# and usage_name. usage itself exits 1 when the command line does not fit the
# spec and 181 when the spec is broken.

# shellcheck shell=bash disable=SC2154 # usage_* are exported by usage
set -euo pipefail
# file lists are enumerated by glob: C-locale order everywhere
export LC_COLLATE=C

# resolve the symlink first: registered with skogai, BASH_SOURCE is the registry link
CONTRACT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(command realpath -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/../contract" && pwd)/usage.sh"
LEVELS=(system global local)
NAME_RE='^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$'
GITROOT=""
STAGE=""
SC_LEVEL=() SC_PATH=() SC_NAME=() SC_DEPS=()

_err() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

_ready() {
    local tool version
    for tool in git yq jq; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { _err "missing tool: $tool"; return 2; }
    done
    # another program named yq would turn every file into "not a module"
    version="$(command yq --version 2>&1)" || true
    [[ "$version" == *mikefarah* ]] || { _err "wrong yq: need mikefarah/yq, found: ${version%%$'\n'*}"; return 2; }
    GITROOT="$(command git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || GITROOT=""
}

# the conf.d directories of a level, in mise's load order; local is empty outside git
_dirs() {
    case "$1" in
    system) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d" ;;
    global) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d" ;;
    local) [[ -z "$GITROOT" ]] || printf '%s\n%s\n' "$GITROOT/.mise/conf.d" "$GITROOT/.config/mise/conf.d" ;;
    esac
}

_index() {
    local i
    for i in "${!LEVELS[@]}"; do
        [[ "${LEVELS[i]}" != "$1" ]] || { printf '%s' "$i"; return; }
    done
}

# a skogai module file: parses as toml and _.skogai is a table with exactly one key
# whose value is a table. prints the name, then the depends_on strings as a JSON
# array; prints nothing for any other file
_info() {
    local doc
    doc="$(command yq -p toml -o json -I0 '.' "$1" 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
    command jq -r '
        if type == "object" and (._ | type) == "object" and (._.skogai | type) == "object"
           and (._.skogai | length) == 1 and (._.skogai | to_entries[0].value | type) == "object"
        then ._.skogai | to_entries[0]
             | .key, ([.value.depends_on? // [] | if type == "array" then .[] | select(type == "string") else empty end] | tojson)
        else empty end' <<<"$doc" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# every installed module file, levels in order, directories in order, names C-sorted
_scan() {
    SC_LEVEL=() SC_PATH=() SC_NAME=() SC_DEPS=()
    local level dir f info name deps
    for level in "${LEVELS[@]}"; do
        while IFS= read -r dir; do
            [[ -d "$dir" ]] || continue
            for f in "$dir"/*.toml; do
                [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
                info="$(_info "$f")"
                [[ -n "$info" ]] || continue
                { IFS= read -r name; IFS= read -r deps; } <<<"$info"
                SC_LEVEL+=("$level") SC_PATH+=("$f") SC_NAME+=("$name") SC_DEPS+=("$deps")
            done
        done < <(_dirs "$level")
    done
}

_line() { # module level path action
    command jq -cn --arg m "$1" --arg l "$2" --arg p "$3" --arg a "$4" \
        '{module: $m, level: $l, path: (if $p == "" then null else $p end), action: $a}'
}

_rejected() { # module level reasons-json
    command jq -cn --arg m "$1" --arg l "$2" --argjson r "$3" \
        '{module: (if $m == "" then null else $m end), level: $l, path: null, action: "rejected", reasons: $r}'
}

# target conf.d: the first directory of the level
_target_dir() {
    local dirs
    mapfile -t dirs < <(_dirs "$1")
    ((${#dirs[@]})) || { _err "the local level needs a git work tree"; return 2; }
    printf '%s' "${dirs[0]}"
}

install() {
    local level="$usage_level" path="$usage_path" src src_dir="" base name="" info tdir ti i files f out verdict reasons
    local action=installed target tname tmp
    _ready || return 2
    if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then
        src_dir="$(cd "$path" && pwd)"
        src="$src_dir/${src_dir##*/}.toml"
        [[ -f "$src" ]] || { _err "no ${src_dir##*/}.toml in $path"; return 2; }
    elif [[ -f "$path" && "${path##*/}" == ?*.toml ]]; then
        src="$path"
    else
        _err "not a module toml file or a module directory: $path"
        return 2
    fi
    base="${src##*/}"
    [[ "$base" != [-.]* ]] || { _err "unusable file name: $base"; return 2; }
    tdir="$(_target_dir "$level")" || return 2
    ti="$(_index "$level")"
    if [[ -n "$src_dir" ]] && compgen -G "$src_dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null; then
        command -v bats >/dev/null || { _err "missing tool: bats"; return 2; }
    fi
    info="$(_info "$src")"
    [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r name <<<"$info"

    # 1. rules: the module among the installed ones, in one checker call
    _scan
    STAGE="$(command mktemp -d)"
    trap 'command rm -rf -- "$STAGE"' EXIT
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        (($(_index "${SC_LEVEL[i]}") <= ti)) || continue
        # the file this install would replace takes no part in the rules
        [[ -n "$name" && "$name" =~ $NAME_RE && "${SC_PATH[i]}" == "$tdir/$name.toml" ]] && continue
        command cp -- "${SC_PATH[i]}" "$STAGE/${SC_PATH[i]##*/}"
    done
    command cp -- "$src" "$STAGE/$base"
    files=()
    for f in "$STAGE"/*.toml; do files+=("${f##*/}"); done
    out="$(cd "$STAGE" && "$CONTRACT" check "${files[@]}")" || { _err "the contract checker failed"; return 2; }
    [[ "$(command jq -s 'length' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null)" == "${#files[@]}" ]] ||
        { _err "unexpected output from the contract checker"; return 2; }
    verdict="$(command jq -r --arg f "$base" 'select(.file == $f) | .verdict' <<<"$out")"
    reasons="$(command jq -c --arg f "$base" 'select(.file == $f) | .reasons' <<<"$out")"
    if [[ "$verdict" != valid ]]; then
        _rejected "$name" "$level" "$reasons"
        return 3
    fi
    # 1b. the same name anywhere else, narrower levels included
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        if [[ "${SC_NAME[i]}" == "$name" && "${SC_PATH[i]}" != "$tdir/$name.toml" ]]; then
            _rejected "$name" "$level" '["duplicate-name"]'
            return 3
        fi
    done
    # 2. tests
    if [[ -n "$src_dir" ]] && compgen -G "$src_dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null; then
        (cd "$src_dir" && command bats "$src_dir/tests") >&2 || {
            _rejected "$name" "$level" '["tests-failed"]'
            return 3
        }
    fi
    # 3. target
    target="$tdir/$name.toml"
    if [[ -e "$target" || -L "$target" ]]; then
        info="$(_info "$target")"
        tname=""
        [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r tname <<<"$info"
        [[ "$tname" == "$name" ]] || { _err "$target exists and is not the module $name"; return 2; }
        if command cmp -s -- "$src" "$target"; then
            _line "$name" "$level" "$target" unchanged
            return 0
        fi
        action=updated
    fi
    command mkdir -p -- "$tdir" || { _err "cannot create $tdir"; return 4; }
    # a name mise does not load, so a half-written file is never read
    tmp="$(command mktemp "$tdir/.install-XXXXXX")" || { _err "cannot write in $tdir"; return 4; }
    command cat -- "$src" >"$tmp" && command chmod 0644 -- "$tmp" && command mv -T -- "$tmp" "$target" || {
        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
        _err "cannot install $target"
        return 4
    }
    _line "$name" "$level" "$target" "$action"
}

uninstall() {
    local level="$usage_level" name="$usage_name" tdir target info tname="" i by=() required
    _ready || return 2
    [[ "$name" =~ $NAME_RE ]] || { _err "bad module name: $name"; return 2; }
    tdir="$(_target_dir "$level")" || return 2
    target="$tdir/$name.toml"
    if [[ ! -e "$target" && ! -L "$target" ]]; then
        _line "$name" "$level" "" absent
        return 0
    fi
    info="$(_info "$target")"
    [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r tname <<<"$info"
    [[ "$tname" == "$name" ]] || { _err "$target is not the module $name"; return 2; }
    _scan
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        [[ "${SC_PATH[i]}" != "$target" ]] || continue
        [[ "$(command jq -r --arg n "$name" 'index($n) != null' <<<"${SC_DEPS[i]}")" == true ]] && by+=("${SC_NAME[i]}")
    done
    if ((${#by[@]})); then
        required="$(printf '%s\n' "${by[@]}" | command jq -Rcs 'split("\n") | map(select(. != "")) | unique')"
        command jq -cn --arg m "$name" --arg l "$level" --argjson r "$required" \
            '{module: $m, level: $l, path: null, action: "rejected", reasons: ["required-by"], required_by: $r}'
        return 3
    fi
    command rm -f -- "$target" || { _err "cannot remove $target"; return 4; }
    _line "$name" "$level" "$target" removed
}

ls() {
    local i
    _ready || return 2
    _scan
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        command jq -cn --arg m "${SC_NAME[i]}" --arg l "${SC_LEVEL[i]}" --arg p "${SC_PATH[i]}" \
            '{module: $m, level: $l, path: $p}'
    done
}

# usage hands over the chosen subcommand instead of calling a function for it
case "${usage_cmd:-}" in
install) install ;;
uninstall) uninstall ;;
ls) ls ;;
*) exec "$0" --help ;;
esac
